senses.gloss: To excuse a small fault or a piece of rudeness in everyday politeness.
examples: *Pardon* me — I didn't mean to interrupt.
He *pardoned* my terrible Spanish and answered in English.
A mistake that small is easily *pardoned*.

senses.gloss: To put something, or yourself, somewhere and leave it there, in informal speech.
examples: *Park* your bags in the hall and come eat.
He *parked* himself on the couch and didn't move all afternoon.
She had *parked* her coffee on the windowsill and forgotten it.

senses.gloss: To leave each other, especially after being together a long time.
examples: They *part* at the corner every morning.
We *parted* on good terms.
Having *parted* from his business partner, he started over alone.

senses.gloss: To succeed in a test or an examination.
examples: You have to *pass* the road test before you can drive alone.
She *passed* the bar exam on her first try.
He has *passed* every class except chemistry.

senses.gloss: To hand or throw something to another person.
examples: Could you *pass* me the salt?
The quarterback *passed* the ball to his left.
The note was *passed* from desk to desk.

senses.gloss: To approve a law or a proposal by an official vote.
examples: The Senate is expected to *pass* the bill this week.
Voters *passed* the measure by a wide margin.
The new rules were *passed* without debate.

senses.gloss: To spend a period of time, or for time itself to go by.
examples: They read old magazines to *pass* the time.
Three hours *passed* before anyone noticed she was gone.
Two weeks have *passed* since her last message.

senses.gloss: To stick something onto a surface with glue or paste.
examples: *Paste* the cutouts onto the poster board.
She *pasted* photos into a scrapbook all evening.
Old flyers had been *pasted* over the windows.

senses.gloss: To be a regular customer of a business, or to support it with your money.
senses.ru: быть постоянным клиентом, пользоваться услугами; покровительствовать
examples: Locals still *patronize* the old diner on Main Street.
She *patronized* the same bookstore for twenty years.
The theater is *patronized* mostly by students.

senses.gloss: To stop a video, a song, or a machine for a moment so that it can start again later.
senses.ru: ставить на паузу, поставить на паузу; приостанавливать, приостановить
examples: *Pause* the movie — I'll be right back.
He *paused* the recording to take a call.
I've *paused* the download until we get better Wi-Fi.

senses.gloss: To give someone a quick, light kiss.
examples: He *pecks* his daughter on the forehead every night.
She *pecked* him on the cheek and ran for the bus.
Having *pecked* his wife goodbye, he hurried out the door.

senses.gloss: For paint, skin, or a surface layer to come away in thin pieces.
examples: The paint *peels* every summer.
My shoulders *peeled* after a day at the beach.
The wallpaper is *peeling* near the ceiling.

senses.gloss: To sit on the edge of something, or to stand high up in a narrow spot.
senses.ru: примоститься, присесть на край; возвышаться (о доме, посёлке)
examples: She *perched* on the arm of the sofa.
The village *perches* on a steep hillside above the river.
A small chapel is *perched* on the cliff over the bay.

senses.gloss: To carry out a task, a duty, or an operation.
examples: The scanner *performs* thousands of checks a minute.
Surgeons *performed* the operation in under an hour.
Every test was *performed* twice.

senses.gloss: To work or do a job at a particular level of quality.
examples: The engine *performs* better at low altitude.
Our team *performed* badly in the second half.
The fund has *performed* well this year.

senses.gloss: To make someone believe that something is true.
examples: Nothing you say will *persuade* me that he is innocent.
The evidence *persuaded* the jury of her guilt.
I am still not *persuaded* by his argument.

senses.gloss: To choose one thing or person out of several.
examples: *Pick* whichever one you like.
They *picked* her for the team.
Have you *picked* a name for the baby yet?

senses.gloss: To pull or scratch small bits off or out of something with your fingers or a point.
examples: Stop *picking* your teeth at the table.
She *picked* a splinter out of her thumb with a needle.
Don't *pick* that scab or it will scar.

senses.gloss: To show someone or something in a photograph, a painting, or a film.
examples: The magazine *pictured* her on the cover.
He is *pictured* here with his two daughters.
The mural *pictures* the town as it looked in 1900.

senses.gloss: To throw something, especially to throw a baseball to the batter.
senses.ru: бросать, бросить; подавать, подать (мяч в бейсболе)
examples: He *pitches* for a minor-league team in Ohio.
She *pitched* the empty can into the trash.
He has *pitched* three shutouts this season.

senses.gloss: To set up a tent or a camp.
examples: We'll *pitch* the tent before it gets dark.
They *pitched* camp beside the river.
The tents were *pitched* in a wide circle.

senses.gloss: To fall suddenly forward, or to rock up and down the way a boat does.
senses.ru: падать вперёд, рухнуть; качать, качаться (о судне)
examples: The boat *pitches* badly in a heavy sea.
He tripped and *pitched* forward onto the gravel.
The plane was *pitching* so hard that nobody could stand up.

senses.gloss: To change to a different strategy or direction, especially in business or politics.
examples: The company decided to *pivot* toward subscriptions.
They *pivoted* from hardware to software after two bad years.
The campaign is *pivoting* to a message about jobs.

senses.gloss: To formally make an order, a bet, or an advertisement.
examples: You can *place* an order online or by phone.
He *placed* a small bet on the last race.
The ad was *placed* in three local papers.

senses.gloss: To remember where you know someone or something from.
examples: I know that face, but I can't *place* it.
It took her a minute to *place* his accent.
He finally *placed* the man as a neighbor from years ago.

senses.gloss: To put something somewhere secretly so that it will be found or will do harm.
examples: Someone *planted* drugs in his car.
The bomb had been *planted* under a bench.
They accused the agency of *planting* false stories in the press.

senses.gloss: To cover a surface thickly with something, especially with posters or pictures.
examples: Volunteers *plaster* the campus with posters every election.
His photo was *plastered* across every front page.
Someone had been *plastering* stickers all over the lamp posts.

senses.gloss: To take part in a game or a sport, or to amuse yourself the way children do.
examples: Do you want to *play* chess?
They *played* two games and lost both.
The kids are *playing* in the yard.

senses.gloss: To act a particular character in a film or a play.
examples: She *plays* the mother in the new series.
He *played* Hamlet twice in college.
The part has been *played* by four different actors.

senses.gloss: To start a recording so that it can be heard or watched.
examples: *Play* the video again from the start.
The DJ *played* the same song three times.
He was *playing* the voicemail for everyone in the office.

senses.gloss: To want or to choose something, used after words like as, what, and wherever.
examples: Sit wherever you *please*.
She has always done exactly as she *pleased*.
You may stay as long as you *please*.

senses.gloss: To mark points or a route on a graph, a chart, or a map.
senses.ru: наносить на график, строить (график); прокладывать, проложить (курс)
examples: *Plot* the results on a graph.
The navigator *plotted* a course around the storm.
Every case has been *plotted* on a city map.

senses.gloss: To pull out hairs or feathers one at a time.
examples: She *plucks* her eyebrows every couple of weeks.
He *plucked* a gray hair out of his beard.
The chicken had already been *plucked* and cleaned.

senses.gloss: To mention a product, a book, or a show publicly in order to promote it.
examples: Every guest gets to *plug* a new project.
She *plugged* her restaurant twice during the interview.
He has been *plugging* the album on every podcast.

senses.gloss: To fall or drop suddenly and steeply.
examples: Temperatures *plunge* after sunset in the desert.
The bus skidded and *plunged* into the river.
Stock prices have *plunged* since the announcement.

senses.gloss: To hunt or catch animals illegally, or on land that is not yours.
examples: Gangs *poach* elephants for their ivory.
He was caught *poaching* deer on state land.
Thousands of rhinos have been *poached* in the last decade.

senses.gloss: To take an employee or a customer away from a rival company.
examples: Big firms *poach* engineers with huge salaries.
They *poached* our best designer last spring.
Half the staff has been *poached* by competitors.

senses.gloss: To improve a piece of work with small final changes.
examples: She spent the weekend *polishing* her essay.
He *polished* the speech until every line worked.
The script still needs to be *polished*.

senses.gloss: To put money, effort, or knowledge together with other people so that everyone can use it.
examples: Let's *pool* our money and buy one big gift.
The families *pooled* their savings to buy the land.
Data is *pooled* from all three hospitals.

senses.gloss: To create a problem, a risk, or a question that someone has to deal with.
examples: The chemicals *pose* a serious risk to workers.
She *posed* a question no one could answer.
The new rules have *posed* a real problem for small farms.
